articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Television Over New Networks (The Impact on SDH on Broadcasting)' (Digest No.1994/131)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Television Over New Networks (The Impact on SDH on Broadcasting) (Digest No.1994/131)
IEE Colloquium on Television Over New Networks (The Impact on SDH on Broadcasting) (Digest No.1994/131)
abstract: The use of SDH networks to carry television signals raises issues of a totally different nature from those that arise with analogue networks. The SDH network has its own timing structure, and this must be reconciled with that of the television signals. 'Mappings' of signals into the SDH structure must be devised. A fixed-frame mapping for video signals is simple to instrument, and might be acceptable where the video sampling frequency is derived from a rubidium reference or the network itself. Otherwise, justification will be required within the container to avoid rates of pointer adjustment well in excess of expected network rates. Clock recovery and signal timing also raise potential problems. These have been discussed and several solutions proposed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Video services via 140 Mbit over SDH
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Television Over New Networks (The Impact on SDH on Broadcasting) (Digest No.1994/131)
abstract: As the new SDH standard becomes widely deployed, increasing numbers of optical transport services at 140 Mbit will be carried entirely or in part over 155 Mbit synchronous optical links. The mechanism of justifying frequency offsets within the SDH network introduces phase quanta at the point of exit for the 140 Mbit signal. Where this 140 Mbit line is carrying video services, excessive phase disturbance during justification events have been found to compromise colour sub carrier jitter standards, resulting in unacceptable video performance. This paper examines the origin of the phase quanta in the synchronous network and shows how this can give rise to phase disturbance in a video service. Desynchronisers are examined and results of a BNR desynchroniser control system are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Broadcast television services in the SDH environment
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Television Over New Networks (The Impact on SDH on Broadcasting) (Digest No.1994/131)
abstract: As a TV service provider, BT is faced with new requirements and technologies. New video formats, and new network technologies can be brought together to provide broadcast TV services that meet today's needs and those of the future through a reasoned migration path. This paper discusses the types of TV services that could be required, and the issues that arise when these are to be transported over networks based upon the synchronous digital hierarchy (SDH).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optical fibre PPM over TV networks
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Television Over New Networks (The Impact on SDH on Broadcasting) (Digest No.1994/131)
abstract: Pulse position modulation (PPM) can exploit the abundant monomode optical fibre bandwidth to offer improved sensitivity. A new PPM PIN-HBT system is proposed for the transport and distribution of digital TV over the optical fibre network. The proposed system is compared with an equivalent PCM sysem and shown to offer a 9.6 dB sensitivity improvement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: PAL and HDTV transmission experiments using SDH networks
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Television Over New Networks (The Impact on SDH on Broadcasting) (Digest No.1994/131)
abstract: The BBC has been studying the use of SDH for internal routeing and external transmission of audio and video signals since the CCITT Recommendations appeared in the late 1980s. A prototype fibre-optic video routeing system was developed in RACE Project 1036 which used a combination of optical wavelength division multiplexing and electrical time-division multiplexing (WTDM). SDH was adopted as the multiplexing standard. Codecs were developed in RACE Project 1081 to allow PAL, HDTV and audio signals to be carried over this and other SDH networks. This paper describes this work and discusses the benefits SDH networks offer broadcasters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
